reference: Sulfidic argillite and polymetallic massive sulfide (title)

description.lithology: Two rows of drill core are visible. Upper row: dark grey to black, fine-grained, massive to weakly foliated/lineated mafic volcanic rock, possibly basalt / basaltic andesite with a slickensided / striated core surface. Lower row: dark blue-grey to black fine-grained mafic volcanic rock with abundant light grey to pale green, sub-centimetre to centimetre scale irregular patches / amygdules and a few larger coalesced light grey patches at the base of the piece; the groundmass is fine-grained with a faint lineation / striation fabric. The core is in a wooden tray with a white plastic liner between the two rows.
description.alteration: Weak to moderate alteration is visible. Upper row shows patchy green to yellow-green and brownish discoloration consistent with chloritic / epidotic alteration and local oxidation along the broken surface. Lower row shows pale green-grey alteration halos around the light patches and a generally chloritic / low-grade greenschist appearance. Intensity is weak to moderate, not pervasive across the whole pieces.
description.mineralization: none visible. No distinct pyrite, chalcopyrite, pyrrhotite, sphalerite, galena or other ore minerals can be confidently identified in the photo resolution.

anomalies.explanation: Top row shows a broken / missing core interval between two pieces with a ~1-2 cm gap and a jagged fracture surface; the right-hand top piece also displays irregular light grey to pinkish veinlets / breccia infill that should be checked in hand specimen.

Lower row core is broken into several pieces with visible fractures at left and right edges and a network of dark fine veinlets cross-cutting the light grey patches at the base of the piece; the core continuity and any vein material should be verified.
